newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: Che Guevara's bones return to Cuba after 30 years.
newsitem.headline: Che Guevara's bones return to Cuba after 30 years.

text.p: The bones of legendary leftist guerrilla Ernesto "Che" Guevara were put in a coffin and flown back to Cuba on Saturday, 30 years after he was shot by Bolivian troops and buried secretly.
Guevara's handless skeleton was dug up last week in a mass grave where he and members of his failed guerrilla movement where dumped in 1967 after they were captured and executed.

The remains of three Cuban guerrilla fighters who died with Guevara were also placed in small wooden coffins draped with Cuban flags and put on a Cuban plane that left Santa Cruz for Havana at 13:30 local time (1730 GMT).

A Cuban guard of honour, including Che's old comrade-in-arms Commander Ramiro Valdez, accompanied the remains aboard for the flight back to the Communist-ruled island, where is still revered as a revolutionary hero.

Several hundred Bolivians, many in tears, bade farewell to Che with tributes of flowers when his bones were removed to be taken to the airport from a Santa Cruz Hospital, where they had been matched with records of his teeth, height and wounds.
The soldiers who executed the revolutionary icon cut off his hands so his fingerprints would prove he was dead.

Bolivian Interior Minister Victor Hugo Canelas presided in silence as Bolivia officially handed over Che's remains to Cuban forensic scientist Jorge Gonzalez, who led the team that found and identified the bones.
Gonzalez said on Friday that he was positive the handless, bullet-scarred skeleton unearthed in the scrubby hills near the town of Vallegrande was that of the bearded revolutionary.
The asthmatic Argentine doctor, who was Fidel Castro's right-hand man during the armed struggle that brought Castro to power in 1959, became an icon for a generation of leftists around the world.

Guevara and his ragged band of rebels trying to export Cuba's armed revolution to South America were hunted down near Vallegrande in October, 1967. Wounded and starving, Guevara was riddled with bullets by a soldier in a schoolroom and his body exhibited to photographers. He was 39.
Cuba said the remains of Guevara and his three Cuban comrades would be received with military honours at San Antonio de los Banos airforce base south of Havana.

His final resting place will be a mausoleum in a square named after him in the central Cuban town of Santa Clara, the scene of a decisive battle led by Guevara during the guerrilla war to overthrow dictator Fulgencio Batista.

Guevara was industry minister and Central Bank president in the early years of the revolution. But the man of action in him led Guevara to leave Cuba and continue fighting, first in the Congo and then in Bolivia.
The search for Guevara's bones began in December 1995 when a retired army general broke three decades of military silence to say he could remember where he ordered Guevara's burial.
But the general failed to locate the spot and initial excavations at an airstrip outside Vallegrande led nowhere. The search was relaunched in May based on new evidence.
Guevara's closest surviving family are his Cuban widow Aleida March and four children, Aleyda, Camilo, Celia and Ernesto.
Bolivia's government honoured a request by Guevara's widow that his bones be returned to Cuba for final burial.
Local residents in Vallegrande had hoped to put his bones in a mausoleum as a tourist attraction.
The remains of two Bolivians and a Peruvian who fought with Guevara were also found in the mass grave and will remain in Bolivia.
"Che" is a common Argentine expression meaning "Hey" and was the nickname his Cuban comrades gave Guevara.
